name: infra_optuna_hpo
title: Optuna search over a torch model: study loop -> epoch loop -> batch loop, then one final retrain
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the HPO driver shape, three loop levels deep
note: A pure precision trap for the leakage family and for the training-mechanics family at once. `StandardScaler` sits four lines below two `train_test_split` calls and is fitted on x_train ONLY (line 80), the validation and test matrices are merely transformed (81-82), and the search selects on the validation split while x_test is touched exactly once, after the search. Two separate training runs and two separate evaluation runs live in one file, and the batch-level helpers take model / loader / optimizer / criterion as parameters from three different call sites - which is the shape that used to lose the training step entirely. MLView reports nothing here, which is correct. What it does do is lose a node in `ip` mode: `--dataflow ip` deletes the `backward()` node at tune.py:108 that `local` draws (57 nodes / 76 edges -> 56 / 69) and emits an untagged_dataflow diagnostic saying the loss `could not be typed`, about the same line local typed. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-09.
stagesObserved: all eight stages present in local mode. In `ip` mode the train lane drops from 13 nodes to 12 and the graph loses 7 edges.

forbidden.why: both train_test_split calls (lines 74 and 76) run BEFORE the scaler is fitted at line 80, and the fit takes x_train, which already carries TRAIN_SPLIT
x_val and x_test reach scaler.transform (lines 81-82), never scaler.fit or fit_transform
there is no cross-validation call in this program; Optuna's study is a search over held-out validation accuracy, not a CV splitter
there is no temporal signal anywhere - no datetime parsing, no sort on a date column and no statsmodels/prophet import
the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 93
the evaluation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 95
no DataLoader in this file passes num_workers at all, and the module ends in `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the training step at line 105
optimizer.step() is called at line 109, after loss.backward() at line 108
the order is zero_grad (105) -> forward (106) -> loss (107) -> backward (108) -> step (109)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
CosineAnnealingLR is epoch-cadence and scheduler.step() is called in final_fit's epoch loop at line 174, not in a batch loop
evaluate() calls model.eval() at line 116 and model.train() at line 124 on the way out; every evaluation in this file goes through it
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 114
the accuracy comparison at line 123 is on model(features).argmax(dim=1), not on raw logits
TunableMLP.forward returns self.head(self.body(x)) - raw logits - and there is no softmax anywhere in this file
both loops move features and labels to DEVICE before the forward (lines 102-103 and 119-120), and the models are moved with .to(DEVICE) at lines 140 and 163
DEVICE is chosen behind torch.cuda.is_available() at line 41; there is no unguarded .cuda()

seed_everything(SEED) at line 190 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all; both splits pass random_state=seed and the Optuna sampler is TPESampler(seed=SEED)
both train_test_split calls pass random_state=seed (lines 75 and 77) and the training DataLoader passes generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(SEED)
TunableMLP.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 53
`blocks` is a plain list while it is being built, but it is splatted into nn.Sequential(*blocks) at line 63 before it is ever assigned to self - which is exactly the documented suppression
torch.save stores model.state_dict() at line 177 and torch.load passes weights_only=True at line 179
